casualties.note: Zero ships of this six-ship cohort sank during the combat of 10 August 1904. This is a sinking count only: it does not mean no damage, no temporary loss of fighting capacity, no retreat, or no later internment. Later Port Arthur losses and separate engagements are excluded.

note:
Partial quantitative review of the Battle of the Yellow Sea on 10 August 1904 (Gregorian). Six ships of Japan’s First Squadron are compared with the six Russian battleships, not with complete fleets. Other squadrons, cruisers, torpedo craft and accompanying vessels remain explicitly unquantified. Counts measure ships, not equal tonnage or fighting power. The two zero loss observations mean only that no ship in the named cohort sank during the combat of 10 August; they do not mean no damage, no retreat or no later operational loss. Mikasa and Tsesarevich are separate non-renderable examples of damaged survivors, not complete damage totals. No later internments, later Port Arthur destruction or losses in other engagements are included, and no personnel deaths are inferred. Existing models are component analogies: the main-line pre-dreadnought represents battleships, including a Japanese cohort that also had two armoured cruisers; protected-cruiser models represent cruiser components of the unquantified complements, not every small craft or auxiliary. Repeated silhouettes do not reconstruct exact classes. Published dates and the inherited event locator are unchanged. Raw imported observations, if present, remain the build pipeline’s responsibility and are not copied into this patch.

Equipment review: the event-level fallback represents the pre-dreadnought battleship family documented by the museum account. Participant-specific profiles illustrate reviewed components; neither this fallback nor repeated models establish the shares of cruisers or small craft or reconstruct an exact ship.
